hero.title: US–Iran Tensions Keep Oil Markets Under Pressure as OPEC+ Meets
hero.description: The US–Iran conflict continues to disrupt energy markets, while OPEC+ meets today against the backdrop of reduced oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Nigeria's Dangote Refinery IPO and major humanitarian and diplomatic developments also dominate the midday news.

featured.title: OPEC+ Meets as Hormuz Disruption Keeps Global Oil Markets on Edge
featured.content: OPEC+ ministers are meeting on Sunday with the group expected to maintain its current oil-production policy for October. The meeting comes as the US–Iran conflict continues to disrupt oil exports and commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude recently settled at $96.28 a barrel, while US crude settled at $91.48, with both benchmarks recording substantial weekly gains.

articles.title: US–Iran fighting continues around key shipping routes
articles.content: US and Iranian forces exchanged fire around vessels near Iran on Saturday. US Central Command said American forces struck three Iranian oil carriers after Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles towards two US Navy ships. Iran also said it targeted several vessels it considered to be using unauthorised routes around the Strait of Hormuz. No American casualties were reported.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran military conflict tanker Strait of Hormuz

articles.title: OPEC+ meets as oil supply risks remain elevated
articles.content: OPEC+ ministers are meeting today and are expected to keep their October production policy unchanged. The group is facing an unusual market environment because the Iran conflict has disrupted oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz while several members are producing below their official targets.
articles.imageQuery: OPEC oil meeting Saudi Arabia Russia crude oil

articles.title: Oil prices remain near $96 as supply concerns persist
articles.content: Brent crude recently settled at $96.28 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate settled at $91.48. Brent gained 7.6% over the week and US crude rose nearly 10%, reflecting continuing concerns about Middle East supply routes and shipping disruption.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil price market barrels

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO approved by Nigeria's SEC
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the planned IPO for Dangote Refinery. The proposed offering involves 4.1 billion shares priced at ₦525 each and could raise about ₦2.15 trillion, or approximately $1.63 billion. The order book is expected to open on September 14.

articles.title: Pipeline incident reportedly leaves at least 37 dead in Nigeria
articles.content: An environmental group says at least 37 people died after allegedly inhaling fumes while attempting to tap an oil pipeline in southern Nigeria. However, the death toll had not been independently confirmed by Nigerian authorities in the Reuters report. RadiantWaves therefore treats the figure as a reported claim rather than a confirmed official death toll.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria oil pipeline community southern Nigeria

articles.title: Nigeria's security crisis continues to concern families
articles.content: Families affected by Nigeria's kidnapping crisis continue to seek information about missing relatives. The continuing uncertainty is increasing pressure on authorities to improve intelligence gathering, coordinated security operations and protection for vulnerable communities.

articles.title: Nepal disaster death toll passes 1,300
articles.content: The humanitarian crisis caused by catastrophic flooding and landslides in Nepal and neighbouring Tibet continues. More than 1,300 people have died and thousands remain missing. Rescue teams are continuing searches in mountainous areas and tunnels where people may still be trapped.

articles.title: Nepal rescue teams continue difficult search operations
articles.content: Rescue operations remain challenging after the August 26 disaster devastated communities and destroyed important infrastructure. A Chinese national was recently rescued alive from a 225-metre tunnel after spending 10 days underground, becoming the third survivor pulled from tunnels in the affected area.

articles.title: Russia says Trump–Putin–Xi meeting has not been ruled out
articles.content: Russia says it has not ruled out a future trilateral meeting involving Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said the agenda and possible outcome would need to be clarified before preparations could begin. The possibility has been linked to the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November.
articles.imageQuery: Putin Trump Xi Jinping diplomatic meeting

articles.title: US and Russia continue contacts over Ukraine
articles.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin held more than three hours of talks with US representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow. Russian officials described the discussions as useful, but there was no announced breakthrough. The US representatives are expected to continue diplomatic contacts with Ukraine.

articles.title: Four killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon
articles.content: Lebanon's health ministry says four people, including two women, were killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Sunday. Israel said the attacks followed alleged Hezbollah drone attacks. The strikes come despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement reached in June.

articles.title: Germany's AfD seeks historic breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt
articles.content: Voting is taking place in Saxony-Anhalt in a closely watched state election. The far-right Alternative for Germany has been polling strongly and could become the first far-right party to lead a German state government since the Second World War.

articles.title: US fuel prices reach record Labor Day weekend levels
articles.content: American motorists are facing unusually high fuel prices during the Labor Day weekend. Reuters reports the national average is expected to reach around $4.03 per gallon, above the previous Labor Day record from 2012, as Middle East tensions keep crude and refined-fuel markets under pressure.

articles.title: AI safety talks planned between US and China
articles.content: The United States and China are preparing tentative talks focused specifically on artificial intelligence safety. Discussions are expected to examine risks including AI-enabled cyberattacks and possible cooperation between technology laboratories.

articles.title: RadiantWaves warns audiences about conflict misinformation
articles.content: The US–Iran conflict has generated a large volume of rapidly circulating videos and claims online. Some footage can be old, mislabelled or AI-generated. RadiantWaves Media encourages audiences to check the source, date, location and independent confirmation before sharing dramatic material.

morningSummary: Sunday's midday edition is dominated by the continuing US–Iran conflict and its effect on global energy supplies. OPEC+ is meeting as oil prices remain elevated, while Nigeria's Dangote Refinery IPO represents a major development for African capital markets. Nepal's humanitarian crisis, renewed violence in southern Lebanon and new diplomatic possibilities involving Russia, the US and China are also being closely watched.
bigQuestion: As conflicts continue to affect oil supplies, food prices and economies around the world, how much longer can the global economy absorb these shocks?
quoteOfTheDay: In uncertain times, staying informed is not fear—it is preparation.
